evals.name: explicit-claims-table-request
evals.prompt: Extract the claims table from design/agent-registry.md.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers; locates Acceptance Criteria section; runs extract.py; emits design/.claims/agent-registry.claims.json and .claims.md; runs coverage.py and reports counts.

evals.name: acceptance-criteria-synonym
evals.prompt: Pull the acceptance criteria out of this design doc into something I can hand to the test team.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers on 'acceptance criteria' phrasing. Default output is the markdown rendering (claims.md); if user mentions Cucumber/SpecFlow downstream, offers Gherkin scaffold.

evals.name: verification-matrix-synonym
evals.prompt: I need a verification matrix for the dispatcher design.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers on 'verification matrix' synonym. Locates dispatcher design doc, extracts AC section into structured table.

evals.name: test-plan-from-spec
evals.prompt: What's the test plan implied by design/auth.md? I want it as a checklist.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers (test plan from spec is in scope). Emits claims.md as the checklist. Notes that the skill produces the worklist but doesn't write the tests themselves.

evals.name: what-would-i-test
evals.prompt: Looking at design/queue.md — what would I actually need to test?
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers despite implicit phrasing. Extracts AC section as the answer. If no AC section, surfaces that and offers to extract from prose with lower-confidence defaults.

evals.name: doc-without-AC-section
evals.prompt: Generate a claims table from this design doc.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers; reads doc; finds no Acceptance Criteria section; stops and offers two paths: (a) user adds the section (frink-design-doc skill) or (b) extracts from prose with all-assumed confidence and explicit caveat.

evals.name: with-gherkin-opt-in
evals.prompt: Extract claims from design/payments.md and also generate Gherkin since we use Cucumber.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers; runs extract.py; runs render.py with --gherkin flag; emits .claims.json, .claims.md, and .feature files.

evals.name: casual-phrasing
evals.prompt: ok now break down the AC into a table
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers; 'AC' is recognized as acceptance criteria; default rendering applied.

evals.name: write-tests-NOT-claims-table
evals.prompt: Write the tests for the agent registry.
evals.expected_output: Skill does NOT trigger. Writing tests is downstream of the claims table; out of scope for this skill.

evals.name: write-step-defs-NOT-claims-table
evals.prompt: Implement the Cucumber step definitions for these scenarios.
evals.expected_output: Skill does NOT trigger. Step definitions are test code; this skill produces the scaffold .feature, not the bindings.

evals.name: design-doc-authoring-NOT-extraction
evals.prompt: Write up the design doc for the auth service.
evals.expected_output: Skill does NOT trigger. That's the frink-design-doc skill's job. Authoring a doc and extracting from it are different workflows.

evals.name: general-testing-strategy-NOT-extraction
evals.prompt: How should I think about testing distributed systems generally?
evals.expected_output: Skill does NOT trigger. Generic testing-strategy advice doesn't have a design doc to extract from; not this skill's domain.

evals.name: modify-source-doc-NOT-extraction
evals.prompt: Update design/registry.md to add a new acceptance criterion.
evals.expected_output: Skill does NOT trigger. Modifying the source doc is upstream of this skill — refer the user to the frink-design-doc skill for amendment.

evals.name: claims-from-readme-NOT-design-doc
evals.prompt: Generate test cases from the README.
evals.expected_output: Skill does NOT trigger. README is not a design doc with structured acceptance criteria; this would just be guessing at requirements from prose. Defer.

evals.name: stale-anchors-flagged
evals.prompt: Re-extract claims from design/registry.md and check if anything is stale.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers; runs extract.py with --resolve-anchors; runs coverage.py; reports any stale Drift or test anchors. Doesn't auto-fix.

evals.name: promote-confidence
evals.prompt: I just landed the tests for the dispatcher design — bump the relevant confidences.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers; re-runs extract.py with --resolve-anchors --apply-rubric on the dispatcher doc. Newly-resolving test_anchors trigger 'asserted' → 'tested' suggestions for confirmation.
